description: A permission block that allows everything but keeps two deny rules, for the commands you never want attempted even inside a container.

steps.description: This keeps a short deny list even with the gates off. The page says `deny` is the right tool for anything you never want attempted, even in this mode, and a deny rule survives the auto flag.

`"*": "allow"` approves everything not denied. Inside `bash`, `"rm -rf *": "deny"` blocks the command that empties the mount faster than you can react, and `"git push --force*": "deny"` blocks the force-push.

steps.question: The page says the force-push rule protects the history on GitHub, the copy the container cannot reach, making it the one thing here that is what?

title: Keeping a Short Deny List
